Hourglass.description: Balanced shoulders and hips with a defined waist — a classic, even silhouette.
Hourglass.why: Pieces that follow the waistline keep the natural balance between your shoulders and hips visible.

Rectangle.description: A straighter silhouette with gentle, even proportions through the shoulders, waist and hips.
Rectangle.why: Volume, texture and waist details add shape and movement to an even, streamlined frame.

Pear.description: Hips and thighs are naturally more prominent than the shoulders, often with a well-defined waist.
Pear.why: Interest at the neckline and shoulders, with easy shapes below, creates a harmonious top-to-bottom balance.

Apple.description: A fuller midsection, often with slimmer legs and shoulders and hips of similar width.
Apple.why: Pieces that skim the midsection and create vertical lines feel comfortable and draw attention to the neckline and legs.

Inverted Triangle.description: Shoulders and upper body are naturally more prominent than the hips.
Inverted Triangle.why: Simple shapes at the shoulders with volume or detail below create a balanced, easy silhouette.

Oval.description: Slightly longer than wide, with soft curves and a gently narrower chin.
Oval.why: Balanced proportions suit most styles, so suggestions focus on highlighting your natural symmetry.

Round.description: Soft curves and fuller cheeks, with length and width that are close to equal.
Round.why: Height at the crown and vertical lines add length, while gentle angles add contrast to rounded features.

Square.description: A broad forehead and defined jawline create a bold, structured look.
Square.why: Soft curves and vertical movement balance strong, angular lines.

Heart.description: A wider forehead and narrower chin create an elegant, tapered shape.
Heart.why: Softness near the forehead and width near the jaw balance a wider upper face.

Diamond.description: High cheekbones with a narrower forehead and chin create a sculpted look.
Diamond.why: Width at the forehead and jaw, with softness at the cheekbones, creates balance.

Oily Skin.description: Oily skin produces more sebum, so the face can look shiny and pores can clog more easily.
focus: Gentle, non-stripping cleansing twice a day

Dry Skin.description: Dry skin has less natural moisture, so it can feel tight, rough or flaky.
focus: Layering hydration on slightly damp skin

Combination Skin.description: Combination skin has oilier areas, usually the T-zone, alongside normal or dry cheeks.
focus: Balancing products that suit both zones
Lighter layers on the T-zone, richer care on dry areas

Normal Skin.description: Normal skin is well balanced, with little dryness, oiliness or sensitivity.

Sensitive Skin.description: Sensitive skin reacts easily to products or weather, with redness, stinging or discomfort.
focus: Introducing one new product at a time after a patch test
Mineral or gentle sunscreen and barrier care

disclaimers.color: Color results are an AI estimate from one selfie. Lighting, camera white balance and makeup can change how undertone appears.
disclaimers.skincare: General information based on your answers, not a medical diagnosis. Patch-test new products and consult a dermatologist for persistent or severe concerns.
disclaimers.face: Based on your questionnaire answers, not a measurement of your face. Face-shape labels don't decide what looks good — use these ideas as a starting point and wear what makes you feel like yourself.
disclaimers.body: Based on your questionnaire answers, not body measurements. Body shape describes proportions only — every shape is a good shape, and these ideas are options, not rules.
